focus_area_title: Prevent and Eliminate Harassment and Discrimination
content_text_body:
Workplace culture is one of the most powerful tools to successfully combat harassment and discrimination, therefore, the company culture can act as the main channel to set and maintain zero-tolerance standards. The goal is to uphold a positive culture where harassment and discrimination are not tolerated. 

To start, assess your current company culture. Ask yourself the following questions: Where does my organization stand on harassment and discrimination issues? How is this incorporated in the company culture? What policies do we have in place that clearly set the stage for non-discriminatory and non-harassment behaviors? Are we abiding by and reinforcing the policies?

### Positive culture 
Trust, empathy and communication are main components in a company culture. Employees who trust one another, feel empathy for one another, and communicate openly with each other can demonstrate greater commitment to cultivating an environment free of harassment and discrimination and would probably feel empowered to speak up and support each other when needed. To further assess your workplace culture, answer the following question: how comfortable are my employees disclosing workplace situations involving harassment and discrimination? 

### Training does not transform culture
Even though awareness trainings can be effective mediums to communicate information, remember it takes more than a harassment and discrimination prevention training session to transform the workplace culture. 

### Leadership on board  
Ensure your leadership is on board with potential updates needed to increase effectiveness for harassment and discrimination policies. Communicate to your employees the importance of sustaining collective strategies to eliminate unacceptable behaviors.  

### Promote resources 
Be sure to communicate to your team how to recognize and report incidents and offer multiple channels for confidential reporting. Consider bringing an outside facilitator/mediator to assist as needed. 

Read this [article](https://hbr.org/2017/12/why-sexual-harassment-persists-and-what-organizations-can-do-to-stop-it) to learn more on why harassment persists on organizations.
